name: HIT catheter robot
full_name: HIT master-slave robotic catheter system for a steerable pull-wire catheter
group: Harbin Institute of Technology, State Key Laboratory of Robotics and System (Yili Fu, Anzhu Gao, Hao Liu, Kai Li, Zhaoguang Liang) with Harbin Medical University
versions: 2008-2010 active/steerable catheter navigation studies (Fu et al., IJMRCAS 2008-2009, titles); 2011 robotic catheter system (fu2011_development, full); 2011 master-slave catheterisation system (fu2011_masterslave, title)
target_anatomy: thoracic/cardiac vessels (thorax vascular phantom, brachiocephalic trunk)
devices_driven: custom 7 Fr single-curve pull-wire steerable catheter with two 5-DOF magnetic tracking sensors, two electrodes and a thermocouple (fu2011_development Sec. III)
rotation_detail: other: both stepping motors at equal speed rotate the whole friction-wheel unit about the catheter (fu2011_development Sec. IV); bending by a lead-screw slide unit moving the handle sleeve
force_sensing: proximal: two force-sensing elements between the inner and outer wheel of the active friction wheel (fu2011_development Fig. 6)
haptics_leader: Novint Falcon 3-DOF handle with force feedback (fu2011_development Fig. 2)
imaging_compat: EM magnetic tracking + MR-derived 3D guiding image (20 slices); intended to reduce X-ray use
validation_detail: thorax vascular phantom (Shelley Medical), catheterisation to the brachiocephalic trunk (fu2011_development Sec. VI)
key_numbers: image-sensor registration error mean 0.19 mm, RMS 0.49 mm, SD 0.46 mm over 700 wall points (fu2011_development Sec. VI, Fig. 9)
